Assessment scope: independent first-pass M2 Code Review of commit48077547 against M1 b805a0b3, complete recording/discovery implementation and changed callers/tests. Current approved Proposal, three-model Design and Delivery identities were inspected and matched. TG-02/TG-03 and M2 apply. Existing M1 judgment is predecessor evidence only; its applicability is restricted for changed subjects. No reviewer implementation, plan, model, activity or work-state edits were made.

Requirement alignment and architecture: the v2-only recording boundary is implemented in request selection, selected store format, targeted construction/query/observation/spans, explicit live/snapshot validation and directly affected selectors. Stored-v1 codec/schema and exclusive operation definitions are removed. Targeted request schema1 and advanced result schema1 remain independent; v2 stored definitions and operation semantics are retained. An independent schema comparison found retained v2 operation definitions unchanged; changes in the targeted schema are removal of v1 operations/branches and current result contract vocabulary. M3 compact/lifecycle engines and M4 public/governing/package guidance remain explicitly pending, so their presence is not treated as a new M2 defect or complete-retirement claim.

Recovery and safety: source loadJournal admits only version2, then validates saved before/candidate manifests, identities, writes and read set using v2. Initial creation with an absent current manifest retains its existing journal-owned basis. Version1/unknown selectors, inconsistent saved records, rewritten origins and third-state targets reject before completion/restoration. Advanced result schema1 is not a journal selector. Inspected existing publisher lock/exclusion, candidate validation, preservation and retry checks, plus adapted v2 persistence and installed-package tests. The changed fixture contains synthetic v2 scenario data with explicit origins; Git rename similarity is not product-record migration. No archive bytes are converted.

Discovery composition: new presence classifier follows both manifests, current JSON, reserved missing-manifest residue, then uninterpreted YAML/non-current exclusion. Explicit IDs use exact coherent snapshots and bypass unrelated enumeration; valid candidates contain only factual v2 identity/revision data. Missing/invalid registered content cannot establish a valid candidate. Configuration keeps its separate schema1, safe YAML parser and non-record placement validation, fixes record-owned templates and removes review-resolution. Inclusive directory/candidate bounds, ordering, fixed safe diagnostics and incomplete scope are present. However, the composed error-collection/final-envelope path has a required correction: multiple invalid directory IDs produce identical redacted diagnostics, which the closed transport diagnostic validator rejects outside the handler. This is an actual public contract failure, not an optional formatting issue.

Independent direct reproduction: created an isolated project with .git and docs/changes/BAD plus docs/changes/OTHER. executeWorkflowContext(['--json']) throws record-store: duplicate identity or path with invalid-input. Invoking the real binary as workflow-context --json exits1, stdout is empty, stderr is Unexpected internal error followed by RL_CLI_INTERNAL. The required outcome is schema2 rejected, exit2, incomplete scope and safe errors. No project files were altered by the reproduction. Source cause is identical invalid-input/path:null/message triples appended by inspect for both invalid IDs, then passed through validateAdvancedEnvelope by validateWorkflowContextResult. A single invalid selector test cannot detect this collection interaction.

Tests and protection disposition: reviewed changed contract/public CLI/adoption/workflow/query/targeted/persistence tests, synthetic fixture and Python wrapper/selector/install proof. Positive stored-v1 representations, broad EntryRef acceptance, front-matter preservation and origin-unavailable behavior are deliberately decontracted, not presumed redundant. Shared representation limits, result snapshot/membership/identity checks, public selectors, persistent failure/recovery, origin/reference and post-completion correction protection remain in current v2 tests. Old workflow-context readiness/projection assertions leave with that replaced interface; current factual discovery tests cover classifier precedence, explicit isolation, symlinks, configuration and inclusive limits. The 8MiB boundary assertions exercise the public result validator with synthetic envelope sizes; they are not three actual 8MiB CLI executions. The public multi-invalid-ID interaction was missing and needs an outcome-focused regression. No blanket reconstruction of thirteen previously deleted historical suites or old behavior is required.

Evidence assessment: m2-v2-only-recording-discovery records final V2 seven complete modules168pass, full npm489pass/0skip, workflow-context32pass, metadata116/query27/selector174/boundary87/cache14, and additional artifact-lifecycle171/governed-wrapper21/npm-package7. Exact schema generation/model/record/whitespace results are structural evidence. These completed runs support their tested surfaces but do not negate the independently reproduced failure. Three initial retirement/discovery red checks are preserved; original historical failed audit/drift retains its old scope. Later unrelated test fixture/configuration edits do not by themselves require rerunning unchanged query/boundary/cache dependencies; actual unchanged-dependency reuse is explicitly bounded in the evidence. No new broad suite was launched by this review.

Checklist: requirement alignment is concern at the schema2 error response; test coverage is concern at multiple invalid IDs; edge/error handling is concern at aggregation/final validation. Architecture, version compatibility within this slice, security/privacy redaction, generated schema parity, scope containment and evidence attribution otherwise support their bounded requirements. No additional necessary owner decision emerged. One implementation-owned correction and independent rereview are required before M2 closeout. M3/M4 remain, followed by a distinct fresh final whole-change Code Review and Verify; no branch/PR/CI/final readiness is claimed.

Deleted baseline engineering paths below are reviewed as removals from b805a0b3, with their actual original identities. They are not represented as current absent-file hashes:

findings.evidence: Medium; M2/TG-03, CLI-SR-23; owning stage implement. workflow-context.js executeWorkflowContext inspect/fail accumulates the same invalid-input diagnostic with path:null for every unsafe change ID. validateWorkflowContextResult then invokes validateAdvancedEnvelope, whose duplicate-diagnostic check throws outside the error handler. Isolated actual binary reproduction with immediate docs/changes/BAD and docs/changes/OTHER yields exit1, empty stdout and RL_CLI_INTERNAL instead of schema2 rejected/exit2. Invalid names are correctly redacted, but repeated redaction produces an invalid emitted envelope.

origin.rationale: The approved factual discovery contract requires explicit safe diagnostics and exit2 for invalid enumeration/candidate input. An expected malformed-project condition currently escapes into an internal failure, so M2 cannot close despite green existing suites.
origin.required_outcome: Preserve safe redaction and fail-closed validation while ensuring all collected errors form a valid bounded schema2 rejection; identical diagnostics may be safely coalesced. Add a real public-command regression with multiple invalid directory IDs that asserts exit2, schema2 rejected, scope.complete false, no payload disclosure and unchanged project bytes. Preserve valid/partial candidate and single-error behavior. Safe correction path: M2 implementation owner fixes collection/serialization and reruns focused regression plus complete affected workflow-context module and required affected proof, then independent M2 rereview. No Design decision or legacy acceptance restoration is needed.

Only review and finding records are authored here.
